This article first appeared on [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3144832/honeywell--solstice-spinoff-served-on-a-silver-platter?utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141).

Honeywell ([NASDAQ:HON](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HON)) is undergoing a major change. It's breaking up its three core segments into different spinoffs. There was a lot of talk when it was announced earlier this year but the noise has gone quiet now. I believe this spinoff provides a great opportunity to get additional exposure to the best performing segments of HON. The first spinoff "Solstice Advanced Materials which will trade under the ticker SOLS recently successfully issued $1 billion in senior notes at a coupon rate of [5.625](https://www.honeywell.com/us/en/press/2025/10/honeywell-board-of-directors-sets-record-date-and-announces-expected-timing-for-spin-off-of-solstice-advanced-materials)%. This low rate speaks to the positive credit profile of the spinoff. With the 1 - 4 share distribution following the spinoff at the end of this month, I'm a buyer of HON. My average cost has only improved, as I've been buying the dip since late July.

## Company Breakup

* [Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with HON.](https://www.gurufocus.com/id/HON?r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141&utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&utm_content=honeywell_-_solstice_spin-off_served_on_a_silver_platter&utm_term=HON)
* [Is HON fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.](https://www.gurufocus.com/dcf-calculator?ticker=HON&r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141&utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&utm_content=honeywell_-_solstice_spin-off_served_on_a_silver_platter&utm_term=HON)

[Earlier](https://advancedmaterials.honeywell.com/us/en/press-releases/2025/02/honeywell-announces-portfolio-update) this year the board of HON announced its intention to spin off the current business into three directions. Automation will remain the core of HON with Aerospace and Advanced Materials going off as individual companies. The first spinoff is set to occur on 30th October which will be for the advanced materials. On October 23rd HON is set to release its [Q3 results](https://investor.honeywell.com/events/event-details/q3-2025-honeywell-earnings-conference-call) which will undoubtedly have an impact on the share price ahead of the spinoff as the market values the segment's performance. I've taken the liberty of analyzing each of the segments to judge the performance and trends and where each might end up in terms of sales a year from now.

**Honeywell Automation**

This will be the core of Honeywell's business after the two spinoffs. Industrial automation and Building automation will be combined into a more streamlined operation. During the last quarter ([Q2 FY2025](https://investor.honeywell.com/static-files/7a6c6b3e-3768-4313-ab4d-e09392b8491b)) the combined sales were $4.206 billion, with the brute of that coming from industrial automation. Margins performance was solid with both growing YoY, but Building automation ending higher at 26.2%. The decline in industrial automation was mostly due to the timing of a large project last year. Actual sales were largely flat instead year-over-year.

According to Fortune Business the automation market will compound at [9.2% annually](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/industry-reports/industrial-automation-market-101589) by 2029. HON has already surpassed this in building automation, but is being offset by weakness in the other segment. Certain years might post higher growth then others and I think we are at the doorstep of a big move upwards. This will come from lower interest rates making the cost of expansion cheaper and a general push to reshore production to America by the current administration.

**Honeywell Aerospace**

The aerospace segment is the second and final spinoff that will occur next year. The segment showed a moderate improvement in sales last quarter, ending at $4.307 billion. However, margins took a hit and fell by 170 bps. The falling margins was the result of cost inflation which more than offset the strong backlog orders and end market growth in both defense and space. This shows that HON is not immune to tariff policies, although the positive market trends are helping off-set a lot of the otherwise higher costs.Global defense and military spendings [grew](https://dsm.forecastinternational.com/2025/06/13/a-new-era-of-global-defense-spending-key-trends-and-whats-ahead/) 8.1% in 2024 and is set to continue this until [2030](https://globalxetfs.eu/defence-tech-shaping-the-future-of-global-security/) reaching $3.3 trillion globally by then. This segment is well positioned to benefit from this.

**Honeywell Energy and Sustainability Solutions**

This is the final segment and what will be the new Solstice company. It was one of the fastest growing last year at 15% and a moderate 6% in organic growth. Much like the aerospace segment margins fell slightly from again cost inflations and customer settlements but was offset by volume growth instead.

On October 8th HON held its [2025](https://investor.honeywell.com/static-files/43b2a767-c043-48f0-a0e3-60a70019dc88) investor day and dedicated a large portion of this to its up and coming spin-off. HON [included](https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/honeywell-spinoff-solstice-continue-ma-playbook-post-separation-2025-10-08/) revenue guidance of $3.75 - $3.85 billion for the segment this year with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 25%. This comes out to $937 - 962 million in EBITDA. Sector average EV/EBITDA is 12.31 on a forward-basis, pinning the EV at $11.5 - $11.8 billion.

Since the financial profile of Solstice is so strong I can see it getting a premium valuation. Cash conversion is incredibly strong at 70.3%. ROIC beats out the sector median of 7.06% by a wide margin. At 1.5x net leverage the risk profile is moderate. Most credit rating firms put it at BB+ which is very solid. This seems to reflect the recently issued senior notes seeing as that occurred on October 1 and this report came about a week later. At 5.625% coupon rate and $1 billion in value Solstice will pay $56.5 million in annual interest expenses.

This has little impact if EBITDA lands in the range I wrote earlier. Capex grew in 2025 to 10% of net sales as it tried to capture more market share in data centers. It will however normalize at the mid-to-single digit of net sales. If it wasn't explained earlier, Solstice is a major play on data center growth seeing as it makes and sells cooling equipment. This is crucial for data centers to keep them up and running at all times. About 72% of sales are in refrigerants and applied solutions with the remaining being electronic and specialty solutions.

End markets are well diversified with HVAC/R and automotive making up the bulk of it. But I'd like to drag your attention to Nuclear/alternative energy which is a massive market opportunity for Solstice. It already has a significant backlog here supported by global nuclear capacity growing by 3x until 2050. Management notes a $10 trillion market opportunity here with $3 trillion worth of investments being poured into nuclear until 2050 to realize this capacity growth.

## Sum Of Parts For Each Spin-Off

Most estimates for HON are in the range of $210 to $290, but importantly, no forecasts suggest any downside from the current trading price. JPMorgan analyst Stephen Tusa made the argument earlier this year that it could be worth $330 per share if broken up as the implied premium for pure-play companies would come in.

A good example of how spin-offs often get a bigger multiple is Kenvue (KVUE) from Johnson & Johnson (JNJ). It started off at a P/E lower than JNJ but quickly surpassed it and gained a large premium. It has since come down following Trump's tariffs on medicine and pills, but the scenario still played out as it normally does with spin-offs. I see the same happening with Solstice once it goes public. I've calculated that Solstice shares are worth about $57 - 59 per share. Since you get one per four shares of HON you own the per HON share value is $14.75 on the high-end.

The aerospace segment had $1.098 billion EBITDA profit last quarter, $4.392 billion per year. TransDigm Group (TDG) is a decent peer comparison, perhaps slightly more niched but it will do. It trades at 19.98x FWD EV/EBITDA which seems slightly rich. 17x seems more fair. This gives it an EV of $87 billion or $115 per share, using 646 million outstanding. The last two segments, which will form HON post-spin-offs, are industrial and building automation. Which had combined sales of $4.206 billion last quarter and a blended EBITDA margin of 22.7%. Annually this is $3.819 billion of EBITDA. Rockwell Automation (ROK) is a great comparison, trading at 23x FWD EV/EBITDA.

This seems rich so I'll use a 20x multiple instead giving me a price target of $118. Combined the sum of all parts is $14.75 + $115 + $118 = $247 per share. This implies an upside of 23.9% from the current stock price. It's not as high as some of the other price targets from analysts, but I think this has to do with the applied multiple to each segment. I am comfortable buying shares in HON with this upside. As the saying goes history never repeats itself, but it often rhymes, hinting at buying pre spin-off often can provide decent returns.

## Solstice Is Undervalued Below $57

I've made EV estimates earlier based on forecasted net sales and EBITDA margins by the management which gave me a range of $11.5 - 11.8 billion. As per the company presentation it will receive $450 million in cash and hold $3 billion worth of debt on the balance sheet, leading to a EV range of $8.95 - 9.25 billion HON currently has 646 million basic shares outstanding, at a 1:4 ratio there would be 161 million shares of Solstice circulating. This implies a fair value stock price of $55 - 57. Its EBITDA margin is well above the sector median of 14.32% which suggests that a premium would be applicable, especially considering the relatively low net leverage it will debut with. I would consider selling off my leftover HON shares and go all in on Solstice depending on how far below this price target it ends up dropping. At $40 per share it would be a no-brainer.

## Risks And Final Words

The biggest risk facing this play is that the market valuations doesn't come through and the premium post spin off is lost. My investment case relies on the fact that the sum of parts is much greater than what is currently reflected in the share price. If this doesn't play out investors might be stuck holding shares at a high cost average depending on the debut price. Poor growth in end markets could also disrupt the investment case. Solstice for instance relies on plenty of growth in data centers but if it faces competition it might be hard to convert this into backlogs. Besides this, cost inflation has been hitting both margins and profits across most segments which is worrisome. But with Solstice at least about 60% of production is done domestically which should minimize these costs.I've followed Honeywell for a long time and got very excited when the announcement came for the break up. This means I get to invest into what segment I like the most which I have to say is the new Solstice. My sum of parts valuation also points to a decent upside once all three companies are trading individually.

# Honeywell - Solstice Spin-Off Served On A Silver Platter

This article first appeared on [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3144832/honeywell--solstice-spinoff-served-on-a-silver-platter?utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141).

Honeywell ([NASDAQ:HON](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HON)) is undergoing a major change. It's breaking up its three core segments into different spinoffs. There was a lot of talk when it was announced earlier this year but the noise has gone quiet now. I believe this spinoff provides a great opportunity to get additional exposure to the best performing segments of HON. The first spinoff "Solstice Advanced Materials which will trade under the ticker SOLS recently successfully issued $1 billion in senior notes at a coupon rate of [5.625](https://www.honeywell.com/us/en/press/2025/10/honeywell-board-of-directors-sets-record-date-and-announces-expected-timing-for-spin-off-of-solstice-advanced-materials)%. This low rate speaks to the positive credit profile of the spinoff. With the 1 - 4 share distribution following the spinoff at the end of this month, I'm a buyer of HON. My average cost has only improved, as I've been buying the dip since late July.

## Company Breakup

* [Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with HON.](https://www.gurufocus.com/id/HON?r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141&utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&utm_content=honeywell_-_solstice_spin-off_served_on_a_silver_platter&utm_term=HON)
* [Is HON fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.](https://www.gurufocus.com/dcf-calculator?ticker=HON&r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141&utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&utm_content=honeywell_-_solstice_spin-off_served_on_a_silver_platter&utm_term=HON)

[Earlier](https://advancedmaterials.honeywell.com/us/en/press-releases/2025/02/honeywell-announces-portfolio-update) this year the board of HON announced its intention to spin off the current business into three directions. Automation will remain the core of HON with Aerospace and Advanced Materials going off as individual companies. The first spinoff is set to occur on 30th October which will be for the advanced materials. On October 23rd HON is set to release its [Q3 results](https://investor.honeywell.com/events/event-details/q3-2025-honeywell-earnings-conference-call) which will undoubtedly have an impact on the share price ahead of the spinoff as the market values the segment's performance. I've taken the liberty of analyzing each of the segments to judge the performance and trends and where each might end up in terms of sales a year from now.

**Honeywell Automation**

This will be the core of Honeywell's business after the two spinoffs. Industrial automation and Building automation will be combined into a more streamlined operation. During the last quarter ([Q2 FY2025](https://investor.honeywell.com/static-files/7a6c6b3e-3768-4313-ab4d-e09392b8491b)) the combined sales were $4.206 billion, with the brute of that coming from industrial automation. Margins performance was solid with both growing YoY, but Building automation ending higher at 26.2%. The decline in industrial automation was mostly due to the timing of a large project last year. Actual sales were largely flat instead year-over-year.

According to Fortune Business the automation market will compound at [9.2% annually](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/industry-reports/industrial-automation-market-101589) by 2029. HON has already surpassed this in building automation, but is being offset by weakness in the other segment. Certain years might post higher growth then others and I think we are at the doorstep of a big move upwards. This will come from lower interest rates making the cost of expansion cheaper and a general push to reshore production to America by the current administration.

**Honeywell Aerospace**

The aerospace segment is the second and final spinoff that will occur next year. The segment showed a moderate improvement in sales last quarter, ending at $4.307 billion. However, margins took a hit and fell by 170 bps. The falling margins was the result of cost inflation which more than offset the strong backlog orders and end market growth in both defense and space. This shows that HON is not immune to tariff policies, although the positive market trends are helping off-set a lot of the otherwise higher costs.Global defense and military spendings [grew](https://dsm.forecastinternational.com/2025/06/13/a-new-era-of-global-defense-spending-key-trends-and-whats-ahead/) 8.1% in 2024 and is set to continue this until [2030](https://globalxetfs.eu/defence-tech-shaping-the-future-of-global-security/) reaching $3.3 trillion globally by then. This segment is well positioned to benefit from this.

**Honeywell Energy and Sustainability Solutions**

This is the final segment and what will be the new Solstice company. It was one of the fastest growing last year at 15% and a moderate 6% in organic growth. Much like the aerospace segment margins fell slightly from again cost inflations and customer settlements but was offset by volume growth instead.

On October 8th HON held its [2025](https://investor.honeywell.com/static-files/43b2a767-c043-48f0-a0e3-60a70019dc88) investor day and dedicated a large portion of this to its up and coming spin-off. HON [included](https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/honeywell-spinoff-solstice-continue-ma-playbook-post-separation-2025-10-08/) revenue guidance of $3.75 - $3.85 billion for the segment this year with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 25%. This comes out to $937 - 962 million in EBITDA. Sector average EV/EBITDA is 12.31 on a forward-basis, pinning the EV at $11.5 - $11.8 billion.

Since the financial profile of Solstice is so strong I can see it getting a premium valuation. Cash conversion is incredibly strong at 70.3%. ROIC beats out the sector median of 7.06% by a wide margin. At 1.5x net leverage the risk profile is moderate. Most credit rating firms put it at BB+ which is very solid. This seems to reflect the recently issued senior notes seeing as that occurred on October 1 and this report came about a week later. At 5.625% coupon rate and $1 billion in value Solstice will pay $56.5 million in annual interest expenses.

This has little impact if EBITDA lands in the range I wrote earlier. Capex grew in 2025 to 10% of net sales as it tried to capture more market share in data centers. It will however normalize at the mid-to-single digit of net sales. If it wasn't explained earlier, Solstice is a major play on data center growth seeing as it makes and sells cooling equipment. This is crucial for data centers to keep them up and running at all times. About 72% of sales are in refrigerants and applied solutions with the remaining being electronic and specialty solutions.

End markets are well diversified with HVAC/R and automotive making up the bulk of it. But I'd like to drag your attention to Nuclear/alternative energy which is a massive market opportunity for Solstice. It already has a significant backlog here supported by global nuclear capacity growing by 3x until 2050. Management notes a $10 trillion market opportunity here with $3 trillion worth of investments being poured into nuclear until 2050 to realize this capacity growth.

## Sum Of Parts For Each Spin-Off

Most estimates for HON are in the range of $210 to $290, but importantly, no forecasts suggest any downside from the current trading price. JPMorgan analyst Stephen Tusa made the argument earlier this year that it could be worth $330 per share if broken up as the implied premium for pure-play companies would come in.

A good example of how spin-offs often get a bigger multiple is Kenvue (KVUE) from Johnson & Johnson (JNJ). It started off at a P/E lower than JNJ but quickly surpassed it and gained a large premium. It has since come down following Trump's tariffs on medicine and pills, but the scenario still played out as it normally does with spin-offs. I see the same happening with Solstice once it goes public. I've calculated that Solstice shares are worth about $57 - 59 per share. Since you get one per four shares of HON you own the per HON share value is $14.75 on the high-end.

The aerospace segment had $1.098 billion EBITDA profit last quarter, $4.392 billion per year. TransDigm Group (TDG) is a decent peer comparison, perhaps slightly more niched but it will do. It trades at 19.98x FWD EV/EBITDA which seems slightly rich. 17x seems more fair. This gives it an EV of $87 billion or $115 per share, using 646 million outstanding. The last two segments, which will form HON post-spin-offs, are industrial and building automation. Which had combined sales of $4.206 billion last quarter and a blended EBITDA margin of 22.7%. Annually this is $3.819 billion of EBITDA. Rockwell Automation (ROK) is a great comparison, trading at 23x FWD EV/EBITDA.

This seems rich so I'll use a 20x multiple instead giving me a price target of $118. Combined the sum of all parts is $14.75 + $115 + $118 = $247 per share. This implies an upside of 23.9% from the current stock price. It's not as high as some of the other price targets from analysts, but I think this has to do with the applied multiple to each segment. I am comfortable buying shares in HON with this upside. As the saying goes history never repeats itself, but it often rhymes, hinting at buying pre spin-off often can provide decent returns.

## Solstice Is Undervalued Below $57

I've made EV estimates earlier based on forecasted net sales and EBITDA margins by the management which gave me a range of $11.5 - 11.8 billion. As per the company presentation it will receive $450 million in cash and hold $3 billion worth of debt on the balance sheet, leading to a EV range of $8.95 - 9.25 billion HON currently has 646 million basic shares outstanding, at a 1:4 ratio there would be 161 million shares of Solstice circulating. This implies a fair value stock price of $55 - 57. Its EBITDA margin is well above the sector median of 14.32% which suggests that a premium would be applicable, especially considering the relatively low net leverage it will debut with. I would consider selling off my leftover HON shares and go all in on Solstice depending on how far below this price target it ends up dropping. At $40 per share it would be a no-brainer.

## Risks And Final Words

The biggest risk facing this play is that the market valuations doesn't come through and the premium post spin off is lost. My investment case relies on the fact that the sum of parts is much greater than what is currently reflected in the share price. If this doesn't play out investors might be stuck holding shares at a high cost average depending on the debut price. Poor growth in end markets could also disrupt the investment case. Solstice for instance relies on plenty of growth in data centers but if it faces competition it might be hard to convert this into backlogs. Besides this, cost inflation has been hitting both margins and profits across most segments which is worrisome. But with Solstice at least about 60% of production is done domestically which should minimize these costs.I've followed Honeywell for a long time and got very excited when the announcement came for the break up. This means I get to invest into what segment I like the most which I have to say is the new Solstice. My sum of parts valuation also points to a decent upside once all three companies are trading individually.

# Honeywell - Solstice Spin-Off Served On A Silver Platter

This article first appeared on [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3144832/honeywell--solstice-spinoff-served-on-a-silver-platter?utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141).

Honeywell ([NASDAQ:HON](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HON)) is undergoing a major change. It's breaking up its three core segments into different spinoffs. There was a lot of talk when it was announced earlier this year but the noise has gone quiet now. I believe this spinoff provides a great opportunity to get additional exposure to the best performing segments of HON. The first spinoff "Solstice Advanced Materials which will trade under the ticker SOLS recently successfully issued $1 billion in senior notes at a coupon rate of [5.625](https://www.honeywell.com/us/en/press/2025/10/honeywell-board-of-directors-sets-record-date-and-announces-expected-timing-for-spin-off-of-solstice-advanced-materials)%. This low rate speaks to the positive credit profile of the spinoff. With the 1 - 4 share distribution following the spinoff at the end of this month, I'm a buyer of HON. My average cost has only improved, as I've been buying the dip since late July.

## Company Breakup

* [Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with HON.](https://www.gurufocus.com/id/HON?r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141&utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&utm_content=honeywell_-_solstice_spin-off_served_on_a_silver_platter&utm_term=HON)
* [Is HON fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.](https://www.gurufocus.com/dcf-calculator?ticker=HON&r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141&utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&utm_content=honeywell_-_solstice_spin-off_served_on_a_silver_platter&utm_term=HON)

[Earlier](https://advancedmaterials.honeywell.com/us/en/press-releases/2025/02/honeywell-announces-portfolio-update) this year the board of HON announced its intention to spin off the current business into three directions. Automation will remain the core of HON with Aerospace and Advanced Materials going off as individual companies. The first spinoff is set to occur on 30th October which will be for the advanced materials. On October 23rd HON is set to release its [Q3 results](https://investor.honeywell.com/events/event-details/q3-2025-honeywell-earnings-conference-call) which will undoubtedly have an impact on the share price ahead of the spinoff as the market values the segment's performance. I've taken the liberty of analyzing each of the segments to judge the performance and trends and where each might end up in terms of sales a year from now.

**Honeywell Automation**

This will be the core of Honeywell's business after the two spinoffs. Industrial automation and Building automation will be combined into a more streamlined operation. During the last quarter ([Q2 FY2025](https://investor.honeywell.com/static-files/7a6c6b3e-3768-4313-ab4d-e09392b8491b)) the combined sales were $4.206 billion, with the brute of that coming from industrial automation. Margins performance was solid with both growing YoY, but Building automation ending higher at 26.2%. The decline in industrial automation was mostly due to the timing of a large project last year. Actual sales were largely flat instead year-over-year.

According to Fortune Business the automation market will compound at [9.2% annually](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/industry-reports/industrial-automation-market-101589) by 2029. HON has already surpassed this in building automation, but is being offset by weakness in the other segment. Certain years might post higher growth then others and I think we are at the doorstep of a big move upwards. This will come from lower interest rates making the cost of expansion cheaper and a general push to reshore production to America by the current administration.

**Honeywell Aerospace**

The aerospace segment is the second and final spinoff that will occur next year. The segment showed a moderate improvement in sales last quarter, ending at $4.307 billion. However, margins took a hit and fell by 170 bps. The falling margins was the result of cost inflation which more than offset the strong backlog orders and end market growth in both defense and space. This shows that HON is not immune to tariff policies, although the positive market trends are helping off-set a lot of the otherwise higher costs.Global defense and military spendings [grew](https://dsm.forecastinternational.com/2025/06/13/a-new-era-of-global-defense-spending-key-trends-and-whats-ahead/) 8.1% in 2024 and is set to continue this until [2030](https://globalxetfs.eu/defence-tech-shaping-the-future-of-global-security/) reaching $3.3 trillion globally by then. This segment is well positioned to benefit from this.

**Honeywell Energy and Sustainability Solutions**

This is the final segment and what will be the new Solstice company. It was one of the fastest growing last year at 15% and a moderate 6% in organic growth. Much like the aerospace segment margins fell slightly from again cost inflations and customer settlements but was offset by volume growth instead.

On October 8th HON held its [2025](https://investor.honeywell.com/static-files/43b2a767-c043-48f0-a0e3-60a70019dc88) investor day and dedicated a large portion of this to its up and coming spin-off. HON [included](https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/honeywell-spinoff-solstice-continue-ma-playbook-post-separation-2025-10-08/) revenue guidance of $3.75 - $3.85 billion for the segment this year with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 25%. This comes out to $937 - 962 million in EBITDA. Sector average EV/EBITDA is 12.31 on a forward-basis, pinning the EV at $11.5 - $11.8 billion.

Since the financial profile of Solstice is so strong I can see it getting a premium valuation. Cash conversion is incredibly strong at 70.3%. ROIC beats out the sector median of 7.06% by a wide margin. At 1.5x net leverage the risk profile is moderate. Most credit rating firms put it at BB+ which is very solid. This seems to reflect the recently issued senior notes seeing as that occurred on October 1 and this report came about a week later. At 5.625% coupon rate and $1 billion in value Solstice will pay $56.5 million in annual interest expenses.

This has little impact if EBITDA lands in the range I wrote earlier. Capex grew in 2025 to 10% of net sales as it tried to capture more market share in data centers. It will however normalize at the mid-to-single digit of net sales. If it wasn't explained earlier, Solstice is a major play on data center growth seeing as it makes and sells cooling equipment. This is crucial for data centers to keep them up and running at all times. About 72% of sales are in refrigerants and applied solutions with the remaining being electronic and specialty solutions.

End markets are well diversified with HVAC/R and automotive making up the bulk of it. But I'd like to drag your attention to Nuclear/alternative energy which is a massive market opportunity for Solstice. It already has a significant backlog here supported by global nuclear capacity growing by 3x until 2050. Management notes a $10 trillion market opportunity here with $3 trillion worth of investments being poured into nuclear until 2050 to realize this capacity growth.

## Sum Of Parts For Each Spin-Off

Most estimates for HON are in the range of $210 to $290, but importantly, no forecasts suggest any downside from the current trading price. JPMorgan analyst Stephen Tusa made the argument earlier this year that it could be worth $330 per share if broken up as the implied premium for pure-play companies would come in.

A good example of how spin-offs often get a bigger multiple is Kenvue (KVUE) from Johnson & Johnson (JNJ). It started off at a P/E lower than JNJ but quickly surpassed it and gained a large premium. It has since come down following Trump's tariffs on medicine and pills, but the scenario still played out as it normally does with spin-offs. I see the same happening with Solstice once it goes public. I've calculated that Solstice shares are worth about $57 - 59 per share. Since you get one per four shares of HON you own the per HON share value is $14.75 on the high-end.

The aerospace segment had $1.098 billion EBITDA profit last quarter, $4.392 billion per year. TransDigm Group (TDG) is a decent peer comparison, perhaps slightly more niched but it will do. It trades at 19.98x FWD EV/EBITDA which seems slightly rich. 17x seems more fair. This gives it an EV of $87 billion or $115 per share, using 646 million outstanding. The last two segments, which will form HON post-spin-offs, are industrial and building automation. Which had combined sales of $4.206 billion last quarter and a blended EBITDA margin of 22.7%. Annually this is $3.819 billion of EBITDA. Rockwell Automation (ROK) is a great comparison, trading at 23x FWD EV/EBITDA.

This seems rich so I'll use a 20x multiple instead giving me a price target of $118. Combined the sum of all parts is $14.75 + $115 + $118 = $247 per share. This implies an upside of 23.9% from the current stock price. It's not as high as some of the other price targets from analysts, but I think this has to do with the applied multiple to each segment. I am comfortable buying shares in HON with this upside. As the saying goes history never repeats itself, but it often rhymes, hinting at buying pre spin-off often can provide decent returns.

## Solstice Is Undervalued Below $57

I've made EV estimates earlier based on forecasted net sales and EBITDA margins by the management which gave me a range of $11.5 - 11.8 billion. As per the company presentation it will receive $450 million in cash and hold $3 billion worth of debt on the balance sheet, leading to a EV range of $8.95 - 9.25 billion HON currently has 646 million basic shares outstanding, at a 1:4 ratio there would be 161 million shares of Solstice circulating. This implies a fair value stock price of $55 - 57. Its EBITDA margin is well above the sector median of 14.32% which suggests that a premium would be applicable, especially considering the relatively low net leverage it will debut with. I would consider selling off my leftover HON shares and go all in on Solstice depending on how far below this price target it ends up dropping. At $40 per share it would be a no-brainer.

## Risks And Final Words

The biggest risk facing this play is that the market valuations doesn't come through and the premium post spin off is lost. My investment case relies on the fact that the sum of parts is much greater than what is currently reflected in the share price. If this doesn't play out investors might be stuck holding shares at a high cost average depending on the debut price. Poor growth in end markets could also disrupt the investment case. Solstice for instance relies on plenty of growth in data centers but if it faces competition it might be hard to convert this into backlogs. Besides this, cost inflation has been hitting both margins and profits across most segments which is worrisome. But with Solstice at least about 60% of production is done domestically which should minimize these costs.I've followed Honeywell for a long time and got very excited when the announcement came for the break up. This means I get to invest into what segment I like the most which I have to say is the new Solstice. My sum of parts valuation also points to a decent upside once all three companies are trading individually.

# Honeywell - Solstice Spin-Off Served On A Silver Platter

This article first appeared on [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3144832/honeywell--solstice-spinoff-served-on-a-silver-platter?utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141).

Honeywell ([NASDAQ:HON](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HON)) is undergoing a major change. It's breaking up its three core segments into different spinoffs. There was a lot of talk when it was announced earlier this year but the noise has gone quiet now. I believe this spinoff provides a great opportunity to get additional exposure to the best performing segments of HON. The first spinoff "Solstice Advanced Materials which will trade under the ticker SOLS recently successfully issued $1 billion in senior notes at a coupon rate of [5.625](https://www.honeywell.com/us/en/press/2025/10/honeywell-board-of-directors-sets-record-date-and-announces-expected-timing-for-spin-off-of-solstice-advanced-materials)%. This low rate speaks to the positive credit profile of the spinoff. With the 1 - 4 share distribution following the spinoff at the end of this month, I'm a buyer of HON. My average cost has only improved, as I've been buying the dip since late July.

## Company Breakup

* [Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with HON.](https://www.gurufocus.com/id/HON?r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141&utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&utm_content=honeywell_-_solstice_spin-off_served_on_a_silver_platter&utm_term=HON)
* [Is HON fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.](https://www.gurufocus.com/dcf-calculator?ticker=HON&r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141&utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&utm_content=honeywell_-_solstice_spin-off_served_on_a_silver_platter&utm_term=HON)

[Earlier](https://advancedmaterials.honeywell.com/us/en/press-releases/2025/02/honeywell-announces-portfolio-update) this year the board of HON announced its intention to spin off the current business into three directions. Automation will remain the core of HON with Aerospace and Advanced Materials going off as individual companies. The first spinoff is set to occur on 30th October which will be for the advanced materials. On October 23rd HON is set to release its [Q3 results](https://investor.honeywell.com/events/event-details/q3-2025-honeywell-earnings-conference-call) which will undoubtedly have an impact on the share price ahead of the spinoff as the market values the segment's performance. I've taken the liberty of analyzing each of the segments to judge the performance and trends and where each might end up in terms of sales a year from now.

**Honeywell Automation**

This will be the core of Honeywell's business after the two spinoffs. Industrial automation and Building automation will be combined into a more streamlined operation. During the last quarter ([Q2 FY2025](https://investor.honeywell.com/static-files/7a6c6b3e-3768-4313-ab4d-e09392b8491b)) the combined sales were $4.206 billion, with the brute of that coming from industrial automation. Margins performance was solid with both growing YoY, but Building automation ending higher at 26.2%. The decline in industrial automation was mostly due to the timing of a large project last year. Actual sales were largely flat instead year-over-year.

According to Fortune Business the automation market will compound at [9.2% annually](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/industry-reports/industrial-automation-market-101589) by 2029. HON has already surpassed this in building automation, but is being offset by weakness in the other segment. Certain years might post higher growth then others and I think we are at the doorstep of a big move upwards. This will come from lower interest rates making the cost of expansion cheaper and a general push to reshore production to America by the current administration.

**Honeywell Aerospace**

The aerospace segment is the second and final spinoff that will occur next year. The segment showed a moderate improvement in sales last quarter, ending at $4.307 billion. However, margins took a hit and fell by 170 bps. The falling margins was the result of cost inflation which more than offset the strong backlog orders and end market growth in both defense and space. This shows that HON is not immune to tariff policies, although the positive market trends are helping off-set a lot of the otherwise higher costs.Global defense and military spendings [grew](https://dsm.forecastinternational.com/2025/06/13/a-new-era-of-global-defense-spending-key-trends-and-whats-ahead/) 8.1% in 2024 and is set to continue this until [2030](https://globalxetfs.eu/defence-tech-shaping-the-future-of-global-security/) reaching $3.3 trillion globally by then. This segment is well positioned to benefit from this.

**Honeywell Energy and Sustainability Solutions**

This is the final segment and what will be the new Solstice company. It was one of the fastest growing last year at 15% and a moderate 6% in organic growth. Much like the aerospace segment margins fell slightly from again cost inflations and customer settlements but was offset by volume growth instead.

On October 8th HON held its [2025](https://investor.honeywell.com/static-files/43b2a767-c043-48f0-a0e3-60a70019dc88) investor day and dedicated a large portion of this to its up and coming spin-off. HON [included](https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/honeywell-spinoff-solstice-continue-ma-playbook-post-separation-2025-10-08/) revenue guidance of $3.75 - $3.85 billion for the segment this year with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 25%. This comes out to $937 - 962 million in EBITDA. Sector average EV/EBITDA is 12.31 on a forward-basis, pinning the EV at $11.5 - $11.8 billion.

Since the financial profile of Solstice is so strong I can see it getting a premium valuation. Cash conversion is incredibly strong at 70.3%. ROIC beats out the sector median of 7.06% by a wide margin. At 1.5x net leverage the risk profile is moderate. Most credit rating firms put it at BB+ which is very solid. This seems to reflect the recently issued senior notes seeing as that occurred on October 1 and this report came about a week later. At 5.625% coupon rate and $1 billion in value Solstice will pay $56.5 million in annual interest expenses.

This has little impact if EBITDA lands in the range I wrote earlier. Capex grew in 2025 to 10% of net sales as it tried to capture more market share in data centers. It will however normalize at the mid-to-single digit of net sales. If it wasn't explained earlier, Solstice is a major play on data center growth seeing as it makes and sells cooling equipment. This is crucial for data centers to keep them up and running at all times. About 72% of sales are in refrigerants and applied solutions with the remaining being electronic and specialty solutions.

End markets are well diversified with HVAC/R and automotive making up the bulk of it. But I'd like to drag your attention to Nuclear/alternative energy which is a massive market opportunity for Solstice. It already has a significant backlog here supported by global nuclear capacity growing by 3x until 2050. Management notes a $10 trillion market opportunity here with $3 trillion worth of investments being poured into nuclear until 2050 to realize this capacity growth.

## Sum Of Parts For Each Spin-Off

Most estimates for HON are in the range of $210 to $290, but importantly, no forecasts suggest any downside from the current trading price. JPMorgan analyst Stephen Tusa made the argument earlier this year that it could be worth $330 per share if broken up as the implied premium for pure-play companies would come in.

A good example of how spin-offs often get a bigger multiple is Kenvue (KVUE) from Johnson & Johnson (JNJ). It started off at a P/E lower than JNJ but quickly surpassed it and gained a large premium. It has since come down following Trump's tariffs on medicine and pills, but the scenario still played out as it normally does with spin-offs. I see the same happening with Solstice once it goes public. I've calculated that Solstice shares are worth about $57 - 59 per share. Since you get one per four shares of HON you own the per HON share value is $14.75 on the high-end.

The aerospace segment had $1.098 billion EBITDA profit last quarter, $4.392 billion per year. TransDigm Group (TDG) is a decent peer comparison, perhaps slightly more niched but it will do. It trades at 19.98x FWD EV/EBITDA which seems slightly rich. 17x seems more fair. This gives it an EV of $87 billion or $115 per share, using 646 million outstanding. The last two segments, which will form HON post-spin-offs, are industrial and building automation. Which had combined sales of $4.206 billion last quarter and a blended EBITDA margin of 22.7%. Annually this is $3.819 billion of EBITDA. Rockwell Automation (ROK) is a great comparison, trading at 23x FWD EV/EBITDA.

This seems rich so I'll use a 20x multiple instead giving me a price target of $118. Combined the sum of all parts is $14.75 + $115 + $118 = $247 per share. This implies an upside of 23.9% from the current stock price. It's not as high as some of the other price targets from analysts, but I think this has to do with the applied multiple to each segment. I am comfortable buying shares in HON with this upside. As the saying goes history never repeats itself, but it often rhymes, hinting at buying pre spin-off often can provide decent returns.

## Solstice Is Undervalued Below $57

I've made EV estimates earlier based on forecasted net sales and EBITDA margins by the management which gave me a range of $11.5 - 11.8 billion. As per the company presentation it will receive $450 million in cash and hold $3 billion worth of debt on the balance sheet, leading to a EV range of $8.95 - 9.25 billion HON currently has 646 million basic shares outstanding, at a 1:4 ratio there would be 161 million shares of Solstice circulating. This implies a fair value stock price of $55 - 57. Its EBITDA margin is well above the sector median of 14.32% which suggests that a premium would be applicable, especially considering the relatively low net leverage it will debut with. I would consider selling off my leftover HON shares and go all in on Solstice depending on how far below this price target it ends up dropping. At $40 per share it would be a no-brainer.

## Risks And Final Words

The biggest risk facing this play is that the market valuations doesn't come through and the premium post spin off is lost. My investment case relies on the fact that the sum of parts is much greater than what is currently reflected in the share price. If this doesn't play out investors might be stuck holding shares at a high cost average depending on the debut price. Poor growth in end markets could also disrupt the investment case. Solstice for instance relies on plenty of growth in data centers but if it faces competition it might be hard to convert this into backlogs. Besides this, cost inflation has been hitting both margins and profits across most segments which is worrisome. But with Solstice at least about 60% of production is done domestically which should minimize these costs.I've followed Honeywell for a long time and got very excited when the announcement came for the break up. This means I get to invest into what segment I like the most which I have to say is the new Solstice. My sum of parts valuation also points to a decent upside once all three companies are trading individually.

I believe this spinoff provides a great opportunity to get additional exposure to the best performing segments of HON. The first spinoff "Solstice Advanced Materials which will trade under the ticker SOLS recently successfully issued $1 billion in senior notes at a coupon rate of [5.625](https://www.honeywell.com/us/en/press/2025/10/honeywell-board-of-directors-sets-record-date-and-announces-expected-timing-for-spin-off-of-solstice-advanced-materials)%. This low rate speaks to the positive credit profile of the spinoff. With the 1 - 4 share distribution following the spinoff at the end of this month, I'm a buyer of HON. My average cost has only improved, as I've been buying the dip since late July.

[Earlier](https://advancedmaterials.honeywell.com/us/en/press-releases/2025/02/honeywell-announces-portfolio-update) this year the board of HON announced its intention to spin off the current business into three directions. Automation will remain the core of HON with Aerospace and Advanced Materials going off as individual companies. The first spinoff is set to occur on 30th October which will be for the advanced materials. On October 23rd HON is set to release its [Q3 results](https://investor.honeywell.com/events/event-details/q3-2025-honeywell-earnings-conference-call) which will undoubtedly have an impact on the share price ahead of the spinoff as the market values the segment's performance. I've taken the liberty of analyzing each of the segments to judge the performance and trends and where each might end up in terms of sales a year from now.

**Honeywell Automation**

This will be the core of Honeywell's business after the two spinoffs. Industrial automation and Building automation will be combined into a more streamlined operation. During the last quarter ([Q2 FY2025](https://investor.honeywell.com/static-files/7a6c6b3e-3768-4313-ab4d-e09392b8491b)) the combined sales were $4.206 billion, with the brute of that coming from industrial automation. Margins performance was solid with both growing YoY, but Building automation ending higher at 26.2%. The decline in industrial automation was mostly due to the timing of a large project last year. Actual sales were largely flat instead year-over-year.

According to Fortune Business the automation market will compound at [9.2% annually](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/industry-reports/industrial-automation-market-101589) by 2029. HON has already surpassed this in building automation, but is being offset by weakness in the other segment. Certain years might post higher growth then others and I think we are at the doorstep of a big move upwards. This will come from lower interest rates making the cost of expansion cheaper and a general push to reshore production to America by the current administration.

**Honeywell Aerospace**

The aerospace segment is the second and final spinoff that will occur next year. The segment showed a moderate improvement in sales last quarter, ending at $4.307 billion. However, margins took a hit and fell by 170 bps. The falling margins was the result of cost inflation which more than offset the strong backlog orders and end market growth in both defense and space. This shows that HON is not immune to tariff policies, although the positive market trends are helping off-set a lot of the otherwise higher costs.Global defense and military spendings [grew](https://dsm.forecastinternational.com/2025/06/13/a-new-era-of-global-defense-spending-key-trends-and-whats-ahead/) 8.1% in 2024 and is set to continue this until [2030](https://globalxetfs.eu/defence-tech-shaping-the-future-of-global-security/) reaching $3.3 trillion globally by then. This segment is well positioned to benefit from this.

**Honeywell Energy and Sustainability Solutions**

This is the final segment and what will be the new Solstice company. It was one of the fastest growing last year at 15% and a moderate 6% in organic growth. Much like the aerospace segment margins fell slightly from again cost inflations and customer settlements but was offset by volume growth instead.

On October 8th HON held its [2025](https://investor.honeywell.com/static-files/43b2a767-c043-48f0-a0e3-60a70019dc88) investor day and dedicated a large portion of this to its up and coming spin-off. HON [included](https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/honeywell-spinoff-solstice-continue-ma-playbook-post-separation-2025-10-08/) revenue guidance of $3.75 - $3.85 billion for the segment this year with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 25%. This comes out to $937 - 962 million in EBITDA. Sector average EV/EBITDA is 12.31 on a forward-basis, pinning the EV at $11.5 - $11.8 billion.

Since the financial profile of Solstice is so strong I can see it getting a premium valuation. Cash conversion is incredibly strong at 70.3%. ROIC beats out the sector median of 7.06% by a wide margin. At 1.5x net leverage the risk profile is moderate. Most credit rating firms put it at BB+ which is very solid. This seems to reflect the recently issued senior notes seeing as that occurred on October 1 and this report came about a week later. At 5.625% coupon rate and $1 billion in value Solstice will pay $56.5 million in annual interest expenses.

This has little impact if EBITDA lands in the range I wrote earlier. Capex grew in 2025 to 10% of net sales as it tried to capture more market share in data centers. It will however normalize at the mid-to-single digit of net sales. If it wasn't explained earlier, Solstice is a major play on data center growth seeing as it makes and sells cooling equipment. This is crucial for data centers to keep them up and running at all times. About 72% of sales are in refrigerants and applied solutions with the remaining being electronic and specialty solutions.

End markets are well diversified with HVAC/R and automotive making up the bulk of it. But I'd like to drag your attention to Nuclear/alternative energy which is a massive market opportunity for Solstice. It already has a significant backlog here supported by global nuclear capacity growing by 3x until 2050. Management notes a $10 trillion market opportunity here with $3 trillion worth of investments being poured into nuclear until 2050 to realize this capacity growth.

## Sum Of Parts For Each Spin-Off

Most estimates for HON are in the range of $210 to $290, but importantly, no forecasts suggest any downside from the current trading price. JPMorgan analyst Stephen Tusa made the argument earlier this year that it could be worth $330 per share if broken up as the implied premium for pure-play companies would come in.

A good example of how spin-offs often get a bigger multiple is Kenvue (KVUE) from Johnson & Johnson (JNJ). It started off at a P/E lower than JNJ but quickly surpassed it and gained a large premium. It has since come down following Trump's tariffs on medicine and pills, but the scenario still played out as it normally does with spin-offs. I see the same happening with Solstice once it goes public. I've calculated that Solstice shares are worth about $57 - 59 per share. Since you get one per four shares of HON you own the per HON share value is $14.75 on the high-end.

The aerospace segment had $1.098 billion EBITDA profit last quarter, $4.392 billion per year. TransDigm Group (TDG) is a decent peer comparison, perhaps slightly more niched but it will do. It trades at 19.98x FWD EV/EBITDA which seems slightly rich. 17x seems more fair. This gives it an EV of $87 billion or $115 per share, using 646 million outstanding. The last two segments, which will form HON post-spin-offs, are industrial and building automation. Which had combined sales of $4.206 billion last quarter and a blended EBITDA margin of 22.7%. Annually this is $3.819 billion of EBITDA. Rockwell Automation (ROK) is a great comparison, trading at 23x FWD EV/EBITDA.

This seems rich so I'll use a 20x multiple instead giving me a price target of $118. Combined the sum of all parts is $14.75 + $115 + $118 = $247 per share. This implies an upside of 23.9% from the current stock price. It's not as high as some of the other price targets from analysts, but I think this has to do with the applied multiple to each segment. I am comfortable buying shares in HON with this upside. As the saying goes history never repeats itself, but it often rhymes, hinting at buying pre spin-off often can provide decent returns.

## Solstice Is Undervalued Below $57

I've made EV estimates earlier based on forecasted net sales and EBITDA margins by the management which gave me a range of $11.5 - 11.8 billion. As per the company presentation it will receive $450 million in cash and hold $3 billion worth of debt on the balance sheet, leading to a EV range of $8.95 - 9.25 billion HON currently has 646 million basic shares outstanding, at a 1:4 ratio there would be 161 million shares of Solstice circulating. This implies a fair value stock price of $55 - 57. Its EBITDA margin is well above the sector median of 14.32% which suggests that a premium would be applicable, especially considering the relatively low net leverage it will debut with. I would consider selling off my leftover HON shares and go all in on Solstice depending on how far below this price target it ends up dropping. At $40 per share it would be a no-brainer.

## Risks And Final Words

The biggest risk facing this play is that the market valuations doesn't come through and the premium post spin off is lost. My investment case relies on the fact that the sum of parts is much greater than what is currently reflected in the share price. If this doesn't play out investors might be stuck holding shares at a high cost average depending on the debut price. Poor growth in end markets could also disrupt the investment case. Solstice for instance relies on plenty of growth in data centers but if it faces competition it might be hard to convert this into backlogs. Besides this, cost inflation has been hitting both margins and profits across most segments which is worrisome. But with Solstice at least about 60% of production is done domestically which should minimize these costs.I've followed Honeywell for a long time and got very excited when the announcement came for the break up. This means I get to invest into what segment I like the most which I have to say is the new Solstice. My sum of parts valuation also points to a decent upside once all three companies are trading individually.

# Honeywell (HON): Valuation Perspectives After Strong Q3, Upbeat Guidance, and New Innovation Moves

Simply Wall St

3 min read

In this article:  

[HON

+1.16%](/quote/HON/ "HON")

Honeywell International (HON) has been in the spotlight after delivering third-quarter 2025 results that topped its own guidance. The results were highlighted by solid organic growth in Aerospace Technologies and stronger Building Automation margins. The company’s moves in quantum computing and retail security also caught investor attention.

[See our latest analysis for Honeywell International.](https://www.simplywall.st/company/id/2f0dc207-79a8-4f1c-9a1c-8db734fc94c8?utm_medium=finance_user&utm_campaign=cta_company_latest_analysis&utm_source=yahoo)

Momentum has stalled for Honeywell’s stock recently, despite headline-grabbing moves in quantum computing and retail security. This article first appeared on [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3144832/honeywell--solstice-spinoff-served-on-a-silver-platter?utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141).

Honeywell ([NASDAQ:HON](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HON)) is undergoing a major change. It's breaking up its three core segments into different spinoffs. There was a lot of talk when it was announced earlier this year but the noise has gone quiet now. I believe this spinoff provides a great opportunity to get additional exposure to the best performing segments of HON. The first spinoff "Solstice Advanced Materials which will trade under the ticker SOLS recently successfully issued $1 billion in senior notes at a coupon rate of [5.625](https://www.honeywell.com/us/en/press/2025/10/honeywell-board-of-directors-sets-record-date-and-announces-expected-timing-for-spin-off-of-solstice-advanced-materials)%. This low rate speaks to the positive credit profile of the spinoff. With the 1 - 4 share distribution following the spinoff at the end of this month, I'm a buyer of HON. My average cost has only improved, as I've been buying the dip since late July.

## Company Breakup

* [Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with HON.](https://www.gurufocus.com/id/HON?r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141&utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&utm_content=honeywell_-_solstice_spin-off_served_on_a_silver_platter&utm_term=HON)
* [Is HON fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.](https://www.gurufocus.com/dcf-calculator?ticker=HON&r=caf6fe0e0db70d936033da5461e60141&utm_source=yahoo_finance&utm_medium=syndication&utm_campaign=headlines&utm_content=honeywell_-_solstice_spin-off_served_on_a_silver_platter&utm_term=HON)

[Earlier](https://advancedmaterials.honeywell.com/us/en/press-releases/2025/02/honeywell-announces-portfolio-update) this year the board of HON announced its intention to spin off the current business into three directions. Automation will remain the core of HON with Aerospace and Advanced Materials going off as individual companies. The first spinoff is set to occur on 30th October which will be for the advanced materials. On October 23rd HON is set to release its [Q3 results](https://investor.honeywell.com/events/event-details/q3-2025-honeywell-earnings-conference-call) which will undoubtedly have an impact on the share price ahead of the spinoff as the market values the segment's performance. I've taken the liberty of analyzing each of the segments to judge the performance and trends and where each might end up in terms of sales a year from now.

**Honeywell Automation**

This will be the core of Honeywell's business after the two spinoffs. Industrial automation and Building automation will be combined into a more streamlined operation. During the last quarter ([Q2 FY2025](https://investor.honeywell.com/static-files/7a6c6b3e-3768-4313-ab4d-e09392b8491b)) the combined sales were $4.206 billion, with the brute of that coming from industrial automation. Margins performance was solid with both growing YoY, but Building automation ending higher at 26.2%. The decline in industrial automation was mostly due to the timing of a large project last year. Actual sales were largely flat instead year-over-year.

According to Fortune Business the automation market will compound at [9.2% annually](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/industry-reports/industrial-automation-market-101589) by 2029. HON has already surpassed this in building automation, but is being offset by weakness in the other segment. Certain years might post higher growth then others and I think we are at the doorstep of a big move upwards. This will come from lower interest rates making the cost of expansion cheaper and a general push to reshore production to America by the current administration.

**Honeywell Aerospace**

The aerospace segment is the second and final spinoff that will occur next year. The segment showed a moderate improvement in sales last quarter, ending at $4.307 billion. However, margins took a hit and fell by 170 bps. The falling margins was the result of cost inflation which more than offset the strong backlog orders and end market growth in both defense and space. This shows that HON is not immune to tariff policies, although the positive market trends are helping off-set a lot of the otherwise higher costs.Global defense and military spendings [grew](https://dsm.forecastinternational.com/2025/06/13/a-new-era-of-global-defense-spending-key-trends-and-whats-ahead/) 8.1% in 2024 and is set to continue this until [2030](https://globalxetfs.eu/defence-tech-shaping-the-future-of-global-security/) reaching $3.3 trillion globally by then. This segment is well positioned to benefit from this.

**Honeywell Energy and Sustainability Solutions**

This is the final segment and what will be the new Solstice company. It was one of the fastest growing last year at 15% and a moderate 6% in organic growth. Much like the aerospace segment margins fell slightly from again cost inflations and customer settlements but was offset by volume growth instead.

On October 8th HON held its [2025](https://investor.honeywell.com/static-files/43b2a767-c043-48f0-a0e3-60a70019dc88) investor day and dedicated a large portion of this to its up and coming spin-off. HON [included](https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/honeywell-spinoff-solstice-continue-ma-playbook-post-separation-2025-10-08/) revenue guidance of $3.75 - $3.85 billion for the segment this year with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 25%. This comes out to $937 - 962 million in EBITDA. Sector average EV/EBITDA is 12.31 on a forward-basis, pinning the EV at $11.5 - $11.8 billion.

Since the financial profile of Solstice is so strong I can see it getting a premium valuation. Cash conversion is incredibly strong at 70.3%. ROIC beats out the sector median of 7.06% by a wide margin. At 1.5x net leverage the risk profile is moderate. Most credit rating firms put it at BB+ which is very solid. This seems to reflect the recently issued senior notes seeing as that occurred on October 1 and this report came about a week later. At 5.625% coupon rate and $1 billion in value Solstice will pay $56.5 million in annual interest expenses.

This has little impact if EBITDA lands in the range I wrote earlier. Capex grew in 2025 to 10% of net sales as it tried to capture more market share in data centers. It will however normalize at the mid-to-single digit of net sales. If it wasn't explained earlier, Solstice is a major play on data center growth seeing as it makes and sells cooling equipment. This is crucial for data centers to keep them up and running at all times. About 72% of sales are in refrigerants and applied solutions with the remaining being electronic and specialty solutions.

End markets are well diversified with HVAC/R and automotive making up the bulk of it. But I'd like to drag your attention to Nuclear/alternative energy which is a massive market opportunity for Solstice. It already has a significant backlog here supported by global nuclear capacity growing by 3x until 2050. Management notes a $10 trillion market opportunity here with $3 trillion worth of investments being poured into nuclear until 2050 to realize this capacity growth.

## Sum Of Parts For Each Spin-Off

Most estimates for HON are in the range of $210 to $290, but importantly, no forecasts suggest any downside from the current trading price. JPMorgan analyst Stephen Tusa made the argument earlier this year that it could be worth $330 per share if broken up as the implied premium for pure-play companies would come in.

A good example of how spin-offs often get a bigger multiple is Kenvue (KVUE) from Johnson & Johnson (JNJ). It started off at a P/E lower than JNJ but quickly surpassed it and gained a large premium. It has since come down following Trump's tariffs on medicine and pills, but the scenario still played out as it normally does with spin-offs. I see the same happening with Solstice once it goes public. I've calculated that Solstice shares are worth about $57 - 59 per share. Since you get one per four shares of HON you own the per HON share value is $14.75 on the high-end.

The aerospace segment had $1.098 billion EBITDA profit last quarter, $4.392 billion per year. TransDigm Group (TDG) is a decent peer comparison, perhaps slightly more niched but it will do. It trades at 19.98x FWD EV/EBITDA which seems slightly rich. 17x seems more fair. This gives it an EV of $87 billion or $115 per share, using 646 million outstanding. The last two segments, which will form HON post-spin-offs, are industrial and building automation. Which had combined sales of $4.206 billion last quarter and a blended EBITDA margin of 22.7%. Annually this is $3.819 billion of EBITDA. Rockwell Automation (ROK) is a great comparison, trading at 23x FWD EV/EBITDA.

This seems rich so I'll use a 20x multiple instead giving me a price target of $118. Combined the sum of all parts is $14.75 + $115 + $118 = $247 per share. This implies an upside of 23.9% from the current stock price. It's not as high as some of the other price targets from analysts, but I think this has to do with the applied multiple to each segment. I am comfortable buying shares in HON with this upside. As the saying goes history never repeats itself, but it often rhymes, hinting at buying pre spin-off often can provide decent returns.

## Solstice Is Undervalued Below $57

I've made EV estimates earlier based on forecasted net sales and EBITDA margins by the management which gave me a range of $11.5 - 11.8 billion. As per the company presentation it will receive $450 million in cash and hold $3 billion worth of debt on the balance sheet, leading to a EV range of $8.95 - 9.25 billion HON currently has 646 million basic shares outstanding, at a 1:4 ratio there would be 161 million shares of Solstice circulating. This implies a fair value stock price of $55 - 57. Its EBITDA margin is well above the sector median of 14.32% which suggests that a premium would be applicable, especially considering the relatively low net leverage it will debut with. I would consider selling off my leftover HON shares and go all in on Solstice depending on how far below this price target it ends up dropping. At $40 per share it would be a no-brainer.

## Risks And Final Words

The biggest risk facing this play is that the market valuations doesn't come through and the premium post spin off is lost. My investment case relies on the fact that the sum of parts is much greater than what is currently reflected in the share price. If this doesn't play out investors might be stuck holding shares at a high cost average depending on the debut price. Poor growth in end markets could also disrupt the investment case. Solstice for instance relies on plenty of growth in data centers but if it faces competition it might be hard to convert this into backlogs. Besides this, cost inflation has been hitting both margins and profits across most segments which is worrisome. But with Solstice at least about 60% of production is done domestically which should minimize these costs.I've followed Honeywell for a long time and got very excited when the announcement came for the break up. This means I get to invest into what segment I like the most which I have to say is the new Solstice. My sum of parts valuation also points to a decent upside once all three companies are trading individually.
